data.name: Village
features: Villagers trade items and have professions
data.howToFind: Use /locate structure minecraft:village_plains (or village_desert, village_savanna, village_taiga, village_snowy). Villages are common in flat biomes and visible from a distance.
dangers: Zombie sieges at night
Raids triggered by Bad Omen effect
Illager patrols near villages
data.notes: Villages generate differently based on their biome. Desert villages use sandstone, taiga villages use spruce wood, and snowy villages use snow and ice blocks. Zombie villages have a 2% chance to generate instead of normal villages.

data.name: Pillager Outpost
data.howToFind: Use /locate structure minecraft:pillager_outpost. They generate near villages in the same biomes. Look for tall dark oak towers on the horizon.
dangers: Continuous pillager spawning
The captain drops an Ominous Bottle that gives Bad Omen
Crossbow attacks from range
rewards: Allays can be freed from cages
data.notes: A pillager captain drops an Ominous Bottle when killed, and drinking it gives the Bad Omen effect, which starts a raid when you enter a village. Allays found in cages can be freed and are useful for item sorting.

data.name: Witch Hut
data.howToFind: Use /locate structure minecraft:swamp_hut. Found exclusively in swamp biomes. Small spruce wood huts on stilts above water.
dangers: Witch throws harmful potions
Swamp terrain is difficult to navigate
rewards: Witch farm potential (only location witches naturally spawn)
data.notes: Witches can spawn in any dark spot, but inside a witch hut's area they are the only mob that can spawn, as long as the whole hut sits in a swamp biome. This makes them valuable for witch farms, which produce redstone, glowstone, and other potion ingredients. The bounding box extends below and around the hut for spawning purposes.

data.name: Desert Pyramid
data.howToFind: Use /locate structure minecraft:desert_pyramid. Found in desert biomes. Large sandstone pyramids are visible from a distance. The treasure room is under the blue terracotta block in the center; dig down beside it so you do not land on the pressure plate.
dangers: TNT trap triggered by pressure plate in treasure room
Can destroy all loot if triggered
Sometimes buried in sand
data.notes: Always mine the pressure plate in the treasure room before stepping on it or the TNT beneath will explode, destroying the chests and loot. The pyramid can sometimes generate partially buried in sand.

data.name: Jungle Pyramid
data.howToFind: Use /locate structure minecraft:jungle_pyramid. Found in jungle biomes. Cobblestone structures overgrown with vines. The dense jungle foliage can make them hard to spot.
dangers: Arrow trap dispensers on the first floor
Tripwire triggers arrow traps
Jungle mobs around the structure
data.notes: The lever puzzle on the bottom floor has three levers wired to a hidden piston; the right combination pulls a block on the main floor away and reveals the hidden chest. Tripwires on the first floor trigger arrow dispensers. Jungle pyramids are rarer than desert pyramids because jungle biomes are less common.

data.name: Woodland Mansion
features: Randomly generated rooms with unique designs
data.howToFind: Use /locate structure minecraft:mansion. Very rare, often thousands of blocks from spawn. Buy a Woodland Explorer Map from a cartographer villager, or use the locate command. Found only in dark forest biomes.
dangers: Vindicators deal heavy melee damage
Evokers summon vexes that fly through walls
Large size means mobs can surprise you
Far from spawn, long trek back
rewards: Large amounts of dark oak wood
Unique room designs for building inspiration
data.notes: Woodland mansions are one of the rarest structures in the game and often generate far from spawn. Evokers always drop a Totem of Undying on death. The mansion contains many unique room types including a fake end portal room, a tree-chopping room, and a map room.

data.name: Igloo
features: Furnished interior with bed and furnace
Basement contains brewing stand and villager/zombie villager
Splash potion of Weakness in brewing stand
uniqueLoot: Splash Potion of Weakness (in brewing stand)
data.howToFind: Use /locate structure minecraft:igloo. Found in snowy biomes. Small white domes that blend in with snowy terrain. Look for a carpet trapdoor inside to find the basement.
dangers: Zombie villager in basement can attack
Easy to miss due to snow camouflage
Cold biome survival challenges
data.notes: The igloo basement is designed to teach players how to cure zombie villagers. It provides everything needed: a golden apple, a splash potion of weakness, and a zombie villager prisoner. Only 50% of igloos have a basement.

data.name: Ruined Portal (Overworld)
features: Can generate underground or on surface
data.howToFind: Use /locate structure minecraft:ruined_portal. Very common throughout the overworld, both on the surface and underground. Look for netherrack patches and crying obsidian.
dangers: Magma blocks deal damage when stood on
Some portals generate underground near lava
rewards: Free obsidian and flint and steel for portal building
data.notes: Ruined portals can be completed with additional obsidian to create a working nether portal. They sometimes contain a gold block that can be mined. The portal frame often contains crying obsidian which cannot be used for portals but is needed for respawn anchors.

data.name: Mineshaft
data.howToFind: Use /locate structure minecraft:mineshaft. Commonly found underground while mining or caving. Look for wooden planks, fences, rails, and cobwebs. In badlands biomes, mineshafts generate at higher elevations and on the surface.
dangers: Cave spider spawners are very dangerous in tight spaces
Cave spiders inflict poison
Dark tunnels with many mob spawns
Easy to get lost in the tunnel network
data.notes: Mineshafts in badlands biomes generate at higher Y-levels and can be exposed on the surface, making them easier to find. Cave spider spawners can be used for XP farms. The tunnel networks can extend for hundreds of blocks.

data.name: Stronghold
features: End portal room with silverfish spawner
Stone brick construction with mossy and cracked variants
data.howToFind: Use /locate structure minecraft:stronghold. Throw Eyes of Ender in the air and follow their direction. They float toward the nearest stronghold and fall when above it. Only 128 strongholds exist per world.
dangers: Silverfish spawner near end portal
Silverfish infested stone bricks
Dark rooms with mob spawns
Getting lost in the maze-like layout
rewards: Access to the End dimension via End Portal
data.notes: There are exactly 128 strongholds per world, arranged in concentric rings around world origin. The first ring has 3 strongholds between 1,280 and 2,816 blocks from the origin. The end portal frame has 12 slots and each has a 10% chance of having an eye of ender already placed.

data.name: Ancient City
features: Sculk blocks and sculk sensors throughout
Ice box room with packed ice
data.howToFind: Use /locate structure minecraft:ancient_city. Found deep underground in the deep dark biome. Mine down to Y -51, where the city floor sits, and look for sculk blocks. Listen for sculk sensor clicks and watch for darkness effect from sculk shriekers.
dangers: Warden is the most dangerous mob in the game (500 HP, can kill in 2 hits)
Sculk shriekers summon the Warden on the fourth shriek
Sculk sensors detect vibrations
Extremely deep underground
Darkness effect reduces visibility
data.notes: The Warden cannot be killed practically in survival mode. It has 500 HP and deals massive damage. The best strategy is stealth: crouch to avoid detection, use wool to muffle sounds, and avoid activating sculk shriekers. Swift Sneak is exclusive to ancient city loot and cannot be obtained elsewhere.

data.name: Trail Ruins
features: Multiple suspicious gravel and sand patches
data.howToFind: Use /locate structure minecraft:trail_ruins. Found buried underground in forested biomes. Look for exposed terracotta or glazed terracotta blocks while mining. Use a brush on suspicious gravel to extract items.
dangers: No hostile mobs, but structure is underground
Easy to accidentally destroy suspicious blocks while mining
rewards: Rare pottery sherds for decorated pots
data.notes: Trail ruins are the primary source for archaeology items. Use a brush (crafted with feather, copper ingot, and stick) on suspicious gravel blocks to extract items. Be careful not to break suspicious blocks with regular tools as the loot will be lost.

data.name: Trial Chamber
features: Trial spawners that scale with player count
Vault blocks that give loot once per player
Multiple room types with different challenges
data.howToFind: Use /locate structure minecraft:trial_chambers. Found underground at deep levels. Listen for the unique sounds of trial spawners. Look for copper and tuff blocks while mining.
dangers: Trial spawners scale difficulty with player count
Breeze mobs knock players around with wind charges
Multiple mob types spawn simultaneously
Ominous trial spawners are significantly harder
rewards: Trial keys unlock vault blocks for exclusive loot
Heavy core for crafting the mace
Wind charges for combat and movement
Exclusive enchantments: Wind Charge, Breach, Density
data.notes: Trial chambers feature a unique mechanic where trial spawners activate when players are nearby and scale with the number of players. Each vault block can only be opened once per player. Drinking an ominous bottle or having Bad Omen converts trial spawners to ominous trial spawners with harder mobs and better vault rewards.

data.name: Amethyst Geode
data.howToFind: Geodes are a world generation feature rather than a structure, so /locate structure cannot find them. Found underground between Y -58 and Y 30. Listen for the chiming sounds of amethyst. Look for smooth basalt shells while mining.
dangers: No specific dangers besides normal underground hazards
rewards: Amethyst shards for spyglass and tinted glass
Calcite and smooth basalt building blocks
data.notes: Budding amethyst blocks cannot be moved or collected even with Silk Touch. They slowly grow amethyst clusters over time, making geodes a renewable source of amethyst shards. Amethyst shards are used to craft spyglass, tinted glass, and calibrated sculk sensors.

data.name: Ocean Monument
data.howToFind: Use /locate structure minecraft:monument. Found in deep ocean biomes. Buy an Ocean Explorer Map from a cartographer villager. Large dark structure visible from the ocean surface with guardians swimming around.
dangers: Mining fatigue from elder guardians (slows mining by 99.7%)
Guardians shoot laser beams
Drowning risk underwater
Three elder guardians to defeat
Must fight underwater
rewards: Sponges from elder guardians and sponge rooms
data.notes: Each ocean monument contains exactly 3 elder guardians. Defeating them removes the Mining Fatigue effect. The gold room contains 8 gold blocks. Sponge rooms may or may not generate. Ocean monuments are popular for guardian farms, which are one of the best XP farms in the game.

data.name: Ocean Ruins
features: Cold ocean variants use stone bricks
data.howToFind: Use /locate structure minecraft:ocean_ruin_cold or minecraft:ocean_ruin_warm. Common on the ocean floor. Dive down and look for stone or sandstone structures with drowned nearby.
dangers: Drowned can carry tridents
Drowning risk while looting
Some ruins are deep underwater
rewards: Sniffer eggs from suspicious sand in warm ruins
data.notes: Warm ocean ruins can contain suspicious sand blocks with sniffer eggs, the only way to get a sniffer before you can breed them. Use a brush to carefully extract items from suspicious sand and gravel. Buried treasure maps point to nearby buried treasure chests.

data.name: Shipwreck
features: Three possible chest locations (bow, stern, map)
Can generate upright, sideways, or upside-down
Can spawn on beaches partially above water
data.howToFind: Use /locate structure minecraft:shipwreck. Common in all ocean biomes and on beaches. Look for wooden structures poking above the ocean surface or visible on the sea floor. Sometimes found beached on coastlines.
dangers: Drowning risk while exploring underwater wrecks
Drowned may spawn nearby
rewards: Buried treasure maps (guaranteed in map chest)
data.notes: Shipwrecks have three possible chests: the supply chest (food), the treasure chest (valuables), and the map chest (always contains a buried treasure map). Not all shipwrecks have all three sections. Shipwrecks on beaches are easy to find and loot without diving.

data.name: Buried Treasure
features: Single chest buried under sand or gravel
Covered by sand, gravel, or stone
data.howToFind: Use /locate structure minecraft:buried_treasure. Follow a Buried Treasure Map from shipwrecks or ocean ruins. The chest is always located at chunk coordinates 9, 9 (press F3 to check). Dig straight down at the X mark on the map.
dangers: Drowning if buried under water
Can be hard to find without map
rewards: Heart of the Sea (for crafting Conduit)
data.notes: The Heart of the Sea is guaranteed in every buried treasure chest and is the key ingredient for crafting a Conduit. Conduits provide water breathing, night vision, and haste while in water. The chest always generates at chunk coordinate 9, 9, making it easy to find with F3.

data.name: Nether Fortress
features: Interior corridors with nether wart farms
data.howToFind: Use /locate structure minecraft:fortress. Each 432 by 432 block region of the Nether holds either a fortress or a bastion remnant, so after finding a bastion, look in a neighboring region. Look for dark nether brick bridges spanning across the nether landscape. Blazes and wither skeletons indicate a fortress is near.
dangers: Blaze fireballs and fire damage
Wither skeletons inflict Wither effect
Falls from bridges into lava
Multiple hostile mobs at once
Open bridges with no railings
rewards: Blaze rods (required for brewing and end portal)
Wither skeleton skulls for summoning the Wither
data.notes: Nether fortresses are essential for game progression as blaze rods are required for brewing stands and crafting eyes of ender. Wither skeleton skulls (rare drop) are needed to summon the Wither boss. Since 1.16 fortresses share their placement with bastion remnants: each 432 by 432 block region gets one of the two, and a fortress is picked 40% of the time.

data.name: Bastion Remnant
features: Four variants: bridge, hoglin stable, housing, treasure
Gold block treasure in treasure variant
Magma cube spawners in treasure variant
data.howToFind: Use /locate structure minecraft:bastion_remnant. Found in all nether biomes except basalt deltas. Large blackstone structures visible from a distance. Listen for piglin and hoglin sounds.
dangers: Piglin brutes cannot be distracted with gold and deal massive damage
Regular piglins attack without gold armor
Hoglins are aggressive
Magma cube spawners in treasure rooms
Lava pools inside structure
data.notes: Bastion remnants are the only source of the Netherite Upgrade Smithing Template, required to upgrade diamond gear to netherite. Piglin brutes cannot be pacified with gold armor and always attack on sight. Wearing gold armor prevents regular piglins from attacking. The treasure bastion variant has the best loot but is heavily guarded.

data.name: Ruined Portal (Nether)
data.howToFind: Use /locate structure minecraft:ruined_portal_nether. Found throughout the Nether dimension. Look for obsidian and crying obsidian portal frames with netherrack platforms.
dangers: Nether environment hazards
Lava nearby
rewards: Flint and steel for portal activation
data.notes: Nether ruined portals use the same loot table as overworld ruined portals. They can be useful for obtaining obsidian to build a return portal if your original portal is destroyed or lost.

data.name: End City
data.howToFind: Use /locate structure minecraft:end_city. After defeating the Ender Dragon, throw an ender pearl into the end gateway portal. End cities generate on the outer end islands. Bridge across void gaps or use elytra from a previously found end ship.
dangers: Shulker levitation effect causes fatal falls
Falling into the void means permanent death
No natural blocks to hide behind
Far from spawn with no easy return
rewards: Shulker shells for shulker boxes (portable storage)
Highly enchanted diamond and iron gear
Purpur blocks and end rods for building
data.notes: Shulker shells are the primary reason to explore end cities, as shulker boxes are the most important storage item in the game. Shulkers have a 50% chance to drop a shell on death, or 68.75% with Looting III. Not all end cities have an end ship attached.

data.name: End Ship
features: Floating ship attached to end city
Brewing stand with instant health potions
data.howToFind: Use /locate structure minecraft:end_city (end ships are attached to end cities). Not all end cities have ships. Look for the ship floating beside the tallest end city tower. Bridge across or use ender pearls to reach it.
dangers: Shulker levitation over the void
Falling into the void
Must navigate the attached end city first
Limited blocks to bridge to the ship
rewards: Elytra (the most valuable item for flight)
data.notes: The elytra is considered one of the most valuable items in Minecraft as it allows the player to glide and, with firework rockets, fly. Not every end city has one: each bridge off a tower has a 12.5% chance of leading to a ship. The elytra is found in an item frame on the ship. The dragon head on the bow opens and closes when powered by redstone.

data.name: End Gateway
features: Generates after defeating the Ender Dragon
One spawns per dragon defeat (up to 20)
Beam of light when first generated
data.howToFind: Defeat the Ender Dragon to spawn an end gateway on the edge of the main end island. Each subsequent dragon respawn and defeat spawns an additional gateway (up to 20). Throw an ender pearl through the bedrock portal to teleport.
dangers: Must defeat the Ender Dragon first
Teleports to potentially dangerous outer islands
Can be hard to aim ender pearl through the small portal
rewards: Access to the outer end islands
Gateway to end cities and end ships
Chorus fruit and chorus flowers on outer islands
data.notes: End gateways are the primary way to reach the outer end islands where end cities generate. Each Ender Dragon defeat creates one gateway, up to a maximum of 20. The gateway teleports the player approximately 1,000 blocks from the main island. Throwing an ender pearl is the intended way to enter the gateway.
